title: Farfalle with Peas and Ham
subtitle: Bow-tie pasta with sweet peas, cooked ham, and a light cream sauce
excerpt: Farfalle with peas and ham is a gentle, mild pasta that cooks in 20 minutes. Frozen peas and cooked ham make it an easy weeknight supper, finished with parmesan and black pepper.
sourceNotes: Italian pasta primavera style; a simple cream-based dish well suited to using frozen peas and leftover or sliced ham.

content.text: Farfalle with peas and ham is a mild, quickly assembled pasta. Frozen peas cook in minutes and keep their colour. The cream sauce is light rather than heavy; just enough to coat the pasta without making the dish stodgy. Add the peas and ham at the end so neither overcooks.

items.prepNote: thickly sliced and cut into strips

content.text: Bring a large pan of salted water to the boil. Cook the farfalle according to the packet. Reserve a mug of pasta water before draining.
Melt the butter in a frying pan over a medium heat. Add the shallots and cook gently for 4 minutes until soft.
Pour in the wine if using. Let it bubble for 1 minute until reduced by half.
Add the cream. Stir and simmer for 2 minutes until it thickens slightly.
Add the peas and ham to the pan. Cook for 2 minutes until the peas are tender and the ham is warmed through.
Add the drained farfalle to the pan with 2 tablespoons of pasta water. Toss everything together over a low heat for 1 minute.
Remove from the heat. Stir in the parmesan and season with black pepper. Scatter over mint if using and serve straight away.

items.cause: The heat was too high once the cream was in the pan.
items.fix: Keep the heat gentle after adding cream; a light simmer thickens it without splitting.

items.cause: They were added too early and overcooked.
items.fix: Add frozen peas only in the last 2 minutes; they go from frozen to bright and tender very quickly.

items.cause: Not enough pasta water was added when tossing.
items.fix: Keep the pasta water close and add a tablespoon at a time until the sauce coats the farfalle loosely.
